title: Effects of a Botanical Extract on Cognitive Performance and Cerebral Blood Flow in Healthy Adults
official: The Acute Effects of Sideritis Scardica (Greek Mountain Tea) on Cognitive Performance and Cerebral Blood Flow in Healthy Adults
summary: The goal of this clinical trial is to learn how a study product affects cognitive performance and cerebral responses in adults. The study will also collect information about the safety of the study product. Participants will attend a screening visit followed by two study visits. During the study visits, participants will complete computerized cognitive assessments before and after consuming the study product and will wear a NIRS headband to record cerebral responses. Researchers will also monitor participants for adverse events and changes in medications or supplements during the study.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Be able to give written informed consent.
2. Be between 18-70 years of age.
3. BMI between 18.5 and 30.0 kg/m2
4. Willing to refrain from consuming alcohol for 24 h, non-habitual stimulants for 18 h prior to Visit 2 (Day 1) and Visit 3 (Day 8).
5. Willing and able to comply with all study procedures and consume the study product as instructed at each study visit.

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Participants who are pregnant or wish to become pregnant during the study or who are lactating and/or currently breastfeeding.
2. Participants currently of biological childbearing potential but not using a continuous effective method of contraception as determined by the investigator.
3. Has a history of drug and/or alcohol abuse (within 12 months prior to visit 1)
4. Participants that are habitual smokers or vapers
5. High caffeine intake, \>400mg/day (approximately equivalent to ≥4 cups of coffee per day
6. Has food allergies, or other issues with foods, that would preclude intake of the study products.
7. Has any significant acute or chronic coexisting health conditions that would prevent them from fulfilling the study requirements, put the Participant at risk or would confound the interpretation of the study results as judged by the investigator on the basis of medical history. Excluded health conditions include:

   1. Uncontrolled hypertension
   2. Clinically significant neurological or mental health conditions (history of stroke/TIA, epilepsy, traumatic brain injury with loss of consciousness, diagnosed ADHD, major depressive disorder within last 6 months)
   3. Diagnosed cognitive impairment
   4. Type I or II diabetes
   5. Clinically significant cardiovascular, liver and renal disease
   6. Diagnosed gastrointestinal conditions (IBD, coeliac disease)
8. Currently or recently taking a medication that the investigator believes would interfere with the objectives of the study or pose a safety risk or confound the interpretation of the study results as judged by the investigator. Prohibited medications include:

   a) Prescription medications such a hypnotic, BDZs, antidepressants, antipsychotics, stimulants, beta-blockers, vasodilators, nootropics, and any psychoactive drugs (in the past 2 weeks prior to visit 1)
9. Current or recent (in the past 2 weeks) use of prohibited nutritional and non-nutritional supplements, that the investigator believes would interfere with the objectives of the study or pose a safety risk or confound the interpretation of the study results as judged by the investigator, including:

   1. Ginseng, ginkgo biloba, Luteolin, Apigenin supplements
   2. Products containing Sideritis, Sage, Thymus and Oregano
10. Individuals who, in the opinion of the investigator, are considered to be poor attendees or unlikely for any reason to be able to comply with the study.
11. Participants may not be participating in other clinical studies. If the participant has previously taken part in an experimental study, the Investigator must ensure sufficient time has elapsed before entry to this study to ensure the integrity of the results.
